Corner-specific waiver, ss_125C_3v00 only (ruling 2026-10-05, answers req-20261005T091748Z-2340426; not Ihsan's own ruling): setup -1.19..-1.20 ns on the vco_out /2 prescaler loop (pre_q0) at the 3.0 ns vco_out period. That period can't occur at ss: sim_pvt run 5 (PASS, analog/reports/gate-sim_pvt.json) puts the VCO top at ~227 MHz (4.4 ns) at ss_125c_vm10 and vco_fmax peaks near 236 MHz (4.24 ns) across all corners, so the VCO never reaches 333 MHz. The /2 loop needs ~4.25 ns at ss, so at the real ss VCO rate it meets with ~0.15 ns; VCO and divider slow together on one die. ff/tt meet at 3.0 ns. Condition: the ~0.15 ns (3.5%) margin must cover VCO period jitter; vco_period_jitter_ps_rms is unmeasured at tt (sim_measure_missing, run 5) and must be measured; revisit if ~6 sigma nears 150 ps. VCO top speed in the spec is NOT lowered. Slew on uo_out[0]/[1] was fixed (clkbuf_8), not waived.

open_issues.note: Not waived. Setup -1.50 ns at ss_125C_3v00 on the vco_out /2 toggle loop (pre_q0 flop _092_) at the new 2.7 ns vco_out period; tt +0.53, ff +1.37. The loop needs ~4.2 ns (238 MHz) at ss. Issue 7's waiver assumed the VCO never passes ~236 MHz at ss; the 31-corner sim_pvt (2026-10-28) shows it does at the skew corner ss_pff (same ss transistors, 125 C, 2.97 V, fast resistors): 290 MHz at vctrl = vdd-0.3 V, 310 MHz at the rail. At the ss grid corners it stays under (ss_125c_vm10 226.9 MHz at the rail). So at ss_pff, if vctrl overshoots above ~2.2 V while acquiring a 200 MHz lock point, the prescaler can drop edges, the loop sees a slow feedback and drives vctrl to the rail: a possible lock-up. Fix options: a faster first prescaler stage (cell choice/drive, or a non-reset flop - changes the P2 decision on async-reset prescaler flops), a VCO clamp at the skew corner (analog), or a rail-recovery/frequency check in the digital. Needs a design decision.
